Container.Name: lore-server
Container.Overview:
Lore is an open source version control system from Epic Games. This is the Lore Server: the central place your team pushes to and clones from.
Auth is off by default. Anyone who can reach this server can read, write and delete every repository. Keep it on your LAN. Do not forward its ports.
With auth off, Lore records every caller as <unknown>. Set Trust unsigned identity to true to record the names people give in the lore CLI and the Lore Web UI. Branches, locks and repositories then show who made them. Lore does not check these names, so anyone can claim any name.
Connect with the lore CLI and the lore:// scheme. Example: lore repository create lore://[your Unraid IP]:41337/my-project
The Repositories folder holds all file content, history and branches. Back it up to back up every repository. The Config folder holds optional settings files. It can stay empty.
To change one setting, add a variable named LORE__ followed by the setting path, such as LORE__SERVER__HTTP__PORT. For settings that need a file, such as a certificate or login, create local.toml in the Config folder and restart the container. Paths in local.toml start with /config. See the Lore Server config reference for every setting.
The server makes a new self-signed certificate each time it starts. lore:// accepts it. lores:// rejects it. To use lores://, put a certificate for your Unraid IP or host name in the Config folder. Your computers must trust it. Set it under both [server.quic.certificate] and [server.grpc.certificate] in local.toml. Then connect with lores:// only.
Docker image by Epic Games.

Config.Name: gRPC port
Config.Description: gRPC, for Lore services. Use the same host port as the QUIC port.

Config.Name: QUIC port
Config.Description: QUIC, for pushes and clones. Use the same host port as the gRPC port.

Config.Name: HTTP port
Config.Description: Health check at /health_check, and HTTP access to file content.

Config.Name: Repositories
Config.Description: All repository data. The immutable folder holds file content and history. The mutable folder holds branches. Big projects need a lot of space, so you can use a share such as /mnt/user/lore.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Optional. Create local.toml here for settings that need a file, such as a certificate or login. Paths in it start with /config. Can stay empty.

Config.Name: Trust unsigned identity
Config.Description: true or false. true records the names people give in the lore CLI and the Lore Web UI. Lore does not check them. Set false if you turn on sign-in in local.toml: the server does not start with both. Overrides the same setting in local.toml.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: error, warn, info, debug or trace.

Config.Name: Config path
Config.Description: Where the server looks for local.toml. Keep as /config.

Config.Name: Content store path
Config.Description: Keeps file content and history in the Repositories folder. Keep as /data.

Config.Name: Branch store path
Config.Description: Keeps branches in the Repositories folder. Keep as /data.
